tools.name: subgraphs_scaffold
tools.description: Generate a subgraph from observed print events when available; ABI token transfers or public functions only when the contract has never printed. Review the TypeScript, run subgraphs_test until ok: true with written >= 1, read skipped, then subgraphs_deploy. dryRun is DDL only.

subgraphName.description: Override the subgraph name (defaults to contract name)

tools.name: subgraphs_list
tools.description: List all deployed subgraphs. Returns summary fields only; read rows with subgraphs_query.

tools.name: subgraphs_status
tools.description: Get full details of a subgraph including schema, health (incl. health.emptyMapping when processed events wrote 0 rows), and table columns.

tools.name: subgraphs_spec
tools.description: Fetch a subgraph's self-describing spec — the tables, columns, filters, and read URLs a consumer needs, without guessing. `agent` (default) returns the compact JSON schema built for tool use, `openapi` the OpenAPI document for the subgraph's read routes, `markdown` human-readable docs. Read it before writing queries against an unfamiliar subgraph.

format.description: agent = JSON schema for tool use (default), openapi = OpenAPI JSON, markdown = docs.md

tools.name: subgraphs_query
tools.description: Query rows from a subgraph table (max 200 rows), reading the open /v1 surface — { rows, next_cursor, tip } envelope, cursor-paginated (no offset). Filters support operators: "amount.gte": "1000", "sender.neq": "SP...", "name.like": "%token%". Available operators: eq, neq, gt, gte, lt, lte, like. Every page with rows returns next_cursor (null only when empty): pass it back as `cursor` to read the next page. To TAIL new rows (no streaming over MCP), poll with cursor = next_cursor ?? the cursor you sent. Fetch one row by id with {"_id": "<id>"}. The same rows are readable over HTTP at GET /v1/subgraphs/<name>/<table>; hand that URL to third parties.

filters.description: Column filters — plain values or with operators (e.g. {"amount.gte": "1000", "sender": "SP..."})

cursor.description: Resume from a previous response's nextCursor

count.description: If true, return row count instead of rows

tools.name: subgraphs_reindex
tools.description: Reindex a subgraph: drops and rebuilds the whole subgraph from its start block to chain tip. Takes no block range — use subgraphs_backfill to process a specific range. Returns an operationId — check subgraphs_status (health) or the REST operations endpoint to track progress to completion.

tools.name: subgraphs_backfill
tools.description: Backfill a subgraph over a block range. Non-destructive forward fill (does not drop existing data) — unlike subgraphs_reindex, and the only data-fill path for BYO subgraphs (reindex is blocked there). Both blocks required. Returns an operationId — check subgraphs_status (health) or the REST operations endpoint to track progress.

tools.name: subgraphs_stop
tools.description: Cancel an in-flight reindex or backfill operation for a subgraph. Returns the stop request status; check subgraphs_status (health) or the REST operations endpoint to confirm it reaches a terminal state.

tools.name: subgraphs_gaps
tools.description: List indexing gaps (missing block ranges) for a subgraph. Each gap reports start/end/size, reason, and detected/resolved timestamps. Feed an unresolved gap's range into subgraphs_backfill to fill it. Defaults to unresolved gaps.

resolved.description: Filter by resolved state (omit for unresolved only)

tools.name: subgraphs_operations
tools.description: Operation history for a subgraph (deploy/reindex/backfill/stop), newest first — status, block range, progress, and error. THIS IS THE VERIFY CALL: after subgraphs_deploy, subgraphs_reindex, subgraphs_backfill, or subgraphs_stop, poll it with the returned operationId until `status` is terminal (completed/failed/cancelled) before reporting success. Omit operationId for the recent history.

operationId.description: Fetch one operation by id (the operationId returned by reindex/backfill/stop); omit for recent history

tools.name: subgraphs_delete
tools.description: Delete a subgraph permanently.

tools.name: subgraphs_deploy
tools.description: Deploy a subgraph from TypeScript code. Pass the full defineSubgraph() source — it will be bundled, validated, and deployed. Optional startBlock overrides the source definition for this deploy. dryRun validates schema/DDL only and does not run handlers — call subgraphs_test first and deploy only when it returns ok: true with written >= 1. Call subgraphs_reindex separately if you need a forced reindex.

code.description: TypeScript source code containing a defineSubgraph() call

startBlock.description: Override the definition startBlock for this deploy

dryRun.description: Validate schema/DDL only — does not run handlers. Use subgraphs_test to prove a mapping writes rows.

tools.name: subgraphs_test
tools.description: Prove a subgraph mapping writes rows against Index data before deploy. Pass full defineSubgraph() source plus a height range. Returns ok/written/tables; EMPTY_MAPPING means events matched but 0 rows were written — read hint for observed event.data keys and do not invent fields. subgraphs_deploy dryRun is DDL only; do not deploy until ok: true with written >= 1.

code.description: TypeScript source containing a defineSubgraph() call

limit.description: Max Index rows per source (default 50, max 200)

tools.name: webhooks_list
tools.description: List all webhooks for the current account. Returns summary fields (no secrets).

tools.name: webhooks_get
tools.description: Get full detail for a webhook (triggers, auth, retry config, circuit state).

tools.name: webhooks_create
tools.description: Create a webhook that fires on raw chain events (set triggers). Returns `signingSecret` ONCE — forward it to the user so they can wire it into their receiver.

triggers.description: Chain triggers. Each targets a raw chain event/tx; string fields accept `*` wildcards, `trait` scopes to a SIP/trait. Per-type accepted fields: see the secondlayer://chain-triggers resource. Forward-looking: starts at chain tip, no backfill.

authConfig.description: Receiver auth sent with each delivery, e.g. {"type": "bearer", "token": "..."}

tools.name: webhooks_update
tools.description: Patch a webhook (name, url, authConfig, format, retry, timeout, concurrency).

authConfig.description: Receiver auth sent with each delivery (bearer/etc.)

tools.name: webhooks_delete
tools.description: Delete a webhook. Pending outbox rows are cascade-deleted.

tools.name: webhooks_test
tools.description: Send a one-off test webhook to a webhook's URL (built for its format, SSRF-guarded). Logged as a delivery row. Returns {ok, statusCode, error, durationMs, deliveryId}.

tools.name: webhooks_pause
tools.description: Pause a webhook: stops delivery attempts and stops queueing new ones. Nothing is deleted — resume picks the webhook back up from the tip. Verify with webhooks_get (status).

tools.name: webhooks_resume
tools.description: Resume a paused webhook (also clears a tripped circuit breaker). Deliveries restart from the current tip — use webhooks_replay for the blocks missed while paused. Verify with webhooks_get (status).

tools.name: webhooks_rotate_secret
tools.description: Rotate a webhook's signing secret. Returns the NEW `signingSecret` ONCE — forward it to the user; deliveries signed with the old secret stop verifying as soon as this returns, so the receiver must be updated.

tools.name: webhooks_deliveries
tools.description: List recent delivery attempts for a webhook — status code, attempt count, error, duration, timestamps. THIS IS THE VERIFY CALL: after webhooks_create, webhooks_test, or webhooks_replay, read it to confirm the webhook actually landed (and to see the receiver's response when it didn't) instead of trusting the enqueue result.

tools.name: webhooks_dead
tools.description: List a webhook's dead-letter queue — deliveries that exhausted their retries, with the outbox id, payload, and last error. Diagnose the receiver first (webhooks_get for the URL/auth, webhooks_test for a live probe), then requeue rows with webhooks_requeue.

tools.name: webhooks_requeue
tools.description: Requeue ONE dead-lettered delivery for another attempt, by its outbox id from webhooks_dead. Fix the receiver first — a requeue against a still-broken endpoint just dies again. Verify with webhooks_deliveries.

outboxId.description: Outbox id of the dead delivery (from webhooks_dead)

tools.name: webhooks_replay
tools.description: Replay a block range for a webhook. Replays run at 10% of batch capacity — use sparingly. Pass `force` (a short idempotency suffix) to re-run a range that was already replayed.

force.description: Idempotency suffix to force a duplicate replay of the range

tools.name: index_ft_transfers
tools.description: List decoded SIP-010 fungible-token transfers from Index. Reads are keyless.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a prior response's next_cursor

order.description: asc (default) reads oldest first; desc reads newest first. A cursor only resumes under the order that issued it.

assetIdentifier.description: Filter by asset identifier (contract::asset), e.g. SP…sbtc-token::sbtc-token

tools.name: index_nft_transfers
tools.description: List decoded SIP-009 non-fungible-token transfers from Index. Reads are keyless.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a prior response's next_cursor

order.description: asc (default) reads oldest first; desc reads newest first. A cursor only resumes under the order that issued it.

tools.name: index_events
tools.description: List decoded chain events from the Index by event type. Use this for event types without a dedicated tool (stx_*, ft_mint/burn, nft_mint/burn, print), and for trait-scoped queries: set `trait` (e.g. sip-010) to match all contracts conforming to a standard — pair with contracts_find to discover traits. For ft/nft transfers without a trait prefer index_ft_transfers / index_nft_transfers.

eventType.description: Required. Decoded event type to list.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a prior response's next_cursor

order.description: asc (default) reads oldest first; desc reads newest first. A cursor only resumes under the order that issued it.

assetIdentifier.description: Filter by asset identifier where applicable

trait.description: Match contracts conforming to a trait/standard (e.g. sip-010). Mutually exclusive with contractId; contract-keyed event types only.

txContext.description: Join the submitting transaction into each event (tx_sender, tx_type, tx_status, tx_contract_id, tx_function_name). For print events it's the only source of the submitting sender.

tools.name: index_contract_calls
tools.description: List decoded contract calls from the Index (function name, args, result). Set `trait` (e.g. sip-010) to match calls to all contracts conforming to a standard. Note: contract-call cursors are a SEPARATE keyspace from event cursors — they are not interchangeable.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a prior response's next_cursor

trait.description: Match contracts conforming to a trait/standard (e.g. sip-010). Mutually exclusive with contractId.

tools.name: index_blocks
tools.description: List decoded blocks from Index. Reads are keyless.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a prior response's next_cursor

tools.name: index_transactions
tools.description: List decoded transactions from Index. Filter by type, sender, or contract. Reads are keyless.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a prior response's next_cursor

tools.name: index_print_schema
tools.description: Empirical per-topic print payload schemas for a contract, inferred from sampled on-chain events: each topic's fields with observed Clarity types, decoded TS types, subgraph column types, and presence rates. Use before writing print_event subgraph handlers to learn what's on e.data. Anonymous read.

contractId.description: Contract id (SP….name) whose print events to profile

tools.name: index_discover
tools.description: Discover the Index vocabulary: every event type and its columns, allowed/equality filters, and required-non-null fields (and which types accept `trait`). Read this before building Index queries instead of guessing filters. Anonymous read.

tools.name: batch_query
tools.description: Run up to 10 public /v1 reads in one round trip (POST /v1/batch). Each item keeps its own auth/quota/pay-per-call semantics; results return in order with per-item status. Paths must start with /v1/index, /v1/subgraphs, /v1/streams, or /v1/contracts.

tools.name: streams_tip
tools.description: Current canonical chain tip as Streams sees it: block height/hash, burn height, finalized_height, lag_seconds, and the oldest seekable height/cursor for this key's retention window. Call it before a cursor walk to know where the stream ends, and after an ingest to check lag.

tools.name: streams_dumps
tools.description: List the Streams bulk parquet dumps manifest — coverage range, latest_finalized_cursor, and per-file metadata (block range, row count, size, sha256, signed URL). This is the cold backfill path for downloading all raw data; fetch the file URLs directly (e.g. with DuckDB). Requires the dumps base URL to be configured (SL_STREAMS_DUMPS_URL). For live reads use REST GET /v1/streams/events; for tip/lag use streams_tip.

tools.name: contracts_find
tools.description: Discover deployed Stacks contracts conforming to a trait (e.g. "sip-010", "sip-009", "sip-013"). The discovery endpoint for "which contracts implement X". Reads are public.

conformance.description: declared = parsed from source, inferred = ABI shape-match, any = either (default)

include.description: Set to "abi" to include each contract's full ABI

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a prior response's next_cursor

tools.name: contracts_get_abi
tools.description: Fetch a single deployed contract's ABI from the registry (prod-safe). Returns the contract's metadata + full ABI (functions, maps, variables, fungible/non-fungible tokens). Returns not_found if the contract isn't in the registry. Use it to inspect a contract before subgraphs_scaffold.

tools.name: codegen_index_schema
tools.description: Generate an ORM schema for the Index tables (blocks, transactions, decoded_events, …) — the same output as `sl codegen index`. Returns the file contents as text; write it wherever your project keeps its schema. Use `tables` to emit only what you read.

tables.description: Restrict to these Index tables (default: all)

schemaName.description: Postgres schema to qualify table names with

datasourceEnv.description: Prisma only: datasource url env var (default DATABASE_URL)

tools.name: instance_status
tools.description: Decoder health and empty-index diagnosis from GET /public/status. If state is empty-index, next tool is archive_bootstrap. Poll until index.decoders are ok before treating Index as ready — do not start decoders. Then archive_verify, then codegen_index_schema. Do not download parquet.

tools.name: archive_verify
tools.description: Read-only, free compare of this instance against a signed archive (POST /v1/archive/verify). unanchored means pin a key or check the URL — not that the instance is fine. After bootstrap, poll instance_status until decoders ok, then this, then codegen_index_schema. Do not download parquet.

tools.name: archive_latest
tools.description: Signed pointer to the official archive tree (hosted). Needs SECONDLAYER_API_KEY (sk-sl_*), not INSTANCE_TOKEN. Use the returned origin as --against for archive_bootstrap. Do not download parquet.

tools.name: archive_quote
tools.description: Price a hosted archive fetch (metered). Needs SECONDLAYER_API_KEY (sk-sl_*), not INSTANCE_TOKEN. Quote happens here; bootstrap/repair also quote inside the CLI. Do not download parquet.

tools.name: credits_balance
tools.description: Archive credits balance at api.secondlayer.tools. Needs SECONDLAYER_API_KEY (sk-sl_*); INSTANCE_TOKEN is the instance.

tools.name: archive_bootstrap
tools.description: Restore verified history into this instance (secondlayer bootstrap --against … --yes --json). Metered against the official archive; quote happens inside the CLI. After bootstrap, poll instance_status until decoders ok, then archive_verify, then codegen_index_schema. Do not download parquet.

fromBlock.description: Restore from this height instead of genesis

toBlock.description: Stop at this height instead of the archive tip

tools.name: archive_repair
tools.description: Plan (default) or apply a repair of local chain data against a signed archive. Metered when apply fetches from the official archive. After apply, poll instance_status until decoders ok, then archive_verify. Do not download parquet.
